minutes_text:
MINUTES

  ADJOURNED

  BUDGET STUDY SESSION

  JUNE 6, 2017

An adjourned meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called
to order at 5:10 p.m. in the Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by
MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF.

2.  ROLL CALL

  City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zuckerman
  City Council Member Absent:  Zerunyan

  City Staff Present: City Manager Doug Prichard
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis

3.  PUBLIC COMMENT

  NONE

4.  ITEMS FOR DISCUSSION

A.  REVIEW OF PROPOSED FISCAL YEAR 2016-17 BUDGET

  Recommendation: That the City Council review the document and discuss the
  programs and services to allow staff to prepare the final budget for presentation
  and public hearing on June 27, 2017.

  City Manager Prichard provided a staff report (as per agenda material) and was
  pleased to note that the City is in a very good financial state and that the
  budget reflects high levels of revenue due to a variety of developments under
  construction. He then updated the COUNCIL on receiving a substantial
  reimbursement from the County for the improvements at the Peter Weber
  Equestrian Center.

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead noted that the County check
  received for the Equestrian Center was in the amount of $650,000 and that
  building permit revenues have been upgraded from $2 million to $2.6 million.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ commented that the City more than likely will not
  see a “spike” in building permits in the future due to fact that the City is now
  essentially built out.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN suggested that the Code Administrator might want
  to inspect a particular neighborhood every week to address those issues that
  might come up as far as illegal construction. Planning Director Wahba
  responded that this department is already overwhelmed and would need an
  additional full-time employee to respond to all those concerns.

  In regards to sales tax, Administrative Services Director Whitehead noted that
  current revenues do not reflect receipts from new businesses such as Orchard
  Supply Hardware as of yet.

ADJOURNED
BUDGET STUDY SESSION
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
JUNE 6, 2017
   Administrative Services Whitehead was pleased to report that the Equestrian
  Fund deficit has been eliminated and that the concessionaire is doing an
  excellent job of operating the Equestrian Center.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN then inquired about what other cities are doing to
  deal with their PERS unfunded liability and the reduction in the discount rate.
  City Manager Prichard responded that many cities have or will be doing what
  the City has done which is pay down certain portions and budget for the
  balance over the term of the amortization period. He noted that the City has
  been ahead of the curve and has the good fortune of not having to deal with
  public safety personnel which significantly increases their PERS liability.

  COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN noted that the City is almost 87.7% funded which
  is outstanding compared to other jurisdictions.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer noted that the City is looking at grants for
  projects regarding Machado Lake and the Sanitation Districts for storm drains
  management.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer then introduced Rex Miller, GIS Analyst II,
  Willdan Engineering, who provided an extensive presentation of the storm drain
  inventory and repairs. Specific drainage issues were also discussed.

  Discussion ensued regarding the difficulties on Buckskin Lane and the cost of
  June’s Trail repairs.

  Discussion ensued regarding the Dapplegray neighborhood’s hesitance to
  accept repairs to their properties. COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ suggested
  scheduling a meeting with MAYOR ZERUNYAN and the neighbors in an effort to
  determine where the homeowners stand.

  It was the consensus of the COUNCIL to follow this approach.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer noted that he will work with the City
  Attorney’s Office in an effort to determine if the same company that performed
  the inspection services could also undertake the repairs since they are familiar
  with the locations. He further noted that the goal is to undertake the repairs
  before the next rainy season.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer noted that catch basin cleaning takes place
  every year, and once the four-year plan to repair the high priority drains is
  complete, inspection will be undertaken for lower priority drains.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report regarding the budget
  impacts on Quimby and Chandler Equestrian Contribution Funds that was
  distributed to the COUNCIL prior to the meeting. He noted that bids were
  received for the Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacon (RRFB) and In-Roadway
  Warning Light (IRWL) Equestrian Crossing Project on Rolling Hills Road/Palos
  Verdes Drive North and the drainage improvements on June’s Trail.

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead noted that initial financing can be
  advanced by the General Fund and then reimbursed when Quimby funds are
  received.

  In response to COUNCILMAN ZUCKERMAN, Planning Director Wahba noted
  that he is looking into consultant assistance to review existing public facility
  impact fees.

  It was the consensus of the COUNCIL to bring both projects forward for
  consideration at a future meeting.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ questioned how many equestrian projects have
  been considered and/or completed as opposed to non-equestrian, and it was
  her desire to include funding for projects that would benefit the entire
  community.
ADJOURNED  2
BUDGET STUDY SESSION
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
JUNE 6, 2017
   COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL explained that the Chandler funds must be spent
  on equestrian-related projects and Quimby funds must be spent on park-
  related projects.

  Community Services Director Clark noted that Proposition A funds will be
  disbursed in 2018 and a number of competitive grants should be available at
  that time.

  City Manager Prichard noted that if the intent is to approve the budget to
  include the two aforementioned projects funded by the General Fund, then they
  will be identified in the budget and brought before the COUNCIL at the public
  hearing scheduled for June 27.

  It was the consensus to follow this approach and bring back award of contracts
  to the next COUNCIL meeting.

  City Manager Prichard reported that the Traffic Control Officer at Rancho Vista
  School will be retiring with no one available to take his place. He noted that
  retention of a part-time employee may be necessary but could prove
  problematic due to the odd schedule, need for training and salary
  considerations.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL suggested utilizing the CORE Deputies for this
  purpose rather than funding Student and the Law classes for Peninsula High
  School. She further suggested contacting the Rolling Hills Covenant Church
  regarding who provides their traffic control on Sundays and coordinate this
  with Chadwick School.

  It was the consensus of the COUNCIL to follow this approach.

  City Manager Prichard provided a staff report on the PERS Obligations (as per
  agenda material). He noted that the City is funded at 87.7% and the trend is
  headed in the right direction as ongoing normal cost contributions have been
  lower due to changes in PERS benefits and retirements. He further noted that
  although the next several years will see substantial increases in UAL and
  normal contributions due to the reduction in the discount rate, the City is as
  well positioned to deal with the increases as any other city. He suggested that
  it might be appropriate to contact KNN Public Finance to assist in analyzing the
  long-term savings options for the City. Finally, he stated that they are
  monitoring this very carefully and are planning accordingly.

5.  ADJOURNMENT

  At 7:38 p.m. MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF formally adjourned the meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Hope J. Nolan  Douglas R. Prichard
Deputy City Clerk  City Clerk
